content: {"summary":"To differentiate lock waits from table bloat on inventory-db-01, examine pg_stat_activity wait_event_type and I/O metrics; lock waits appear as `Lock` events with many sessions blocked by the same pid, while bloat shows as `IO` waits, sequential scans and high shared‑read buffer usage.","likely_cause":"Lock waits are indicated by `Lock` wait events; table bloat is indicated by `IO` waits and high I/O buffer reads.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"Lock waits appear as `Lock` events with many rows blocked by the same pid.","evidence_ids":["RB-015#3"],"quote":"`Lock`, many rows blocked by the same pid."},{"text":"`IO` waits everywhere signal storage latency, a symptom of table bloat.","evidence_ids":["RB-015#4"],"quote":"`IO` waits everywhere. Storage latency on the VM."},{"text":"High shared‑read buffer usage and sequential scans point to table bloat.","evidence_ids":["RB-015#2"],"quote":"Plan looks fine, and the time is in I/O (high `shared read` in BUFFERS)."},{"text":"The June 2025 slowdown showed lock waits on the reservations table.","evidence_ids":["INC-0049#0"],"quote":"The sessions showed lock waits on the `reservations` table."}],"next_checks":["Run the query from RB-015#3 to list wait_event_type and blocked_by for inventory_app sessions.","If wait_event_type is `Lock`, investigate the blocking pid’s query.","If wait_event_type is `IO`, check storage latency metrics and buffer read stats.","Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the slow statements to see sequential scans and shared read counts.","Check pg_stat_user_tables for bloat indicators (e.g., high dead_tuple_pct).","Consider using pgstattuple or pg_repack if bloat is confirmed."]}
